what: Unsolved AC rows whose start presentation lies in the AC class of AK(3) = <x,y | x^3 y^-4, xyx y^-1 x^-1 y^-1>, an open problem. Solving any of them solves AK(3). Skip them in all searches.
source: acwindow-lean evidence/genus/house_walk_L26_members.json.gz (exhaustive walk of the AK(3) class up to total length 26, 1,284,411 members; seeds AK(3), MS(3,yx^2y), MS(3,y^-1x^2y^-1)). Moves of the walk: cyclic rotation, inversion, relabelling by the 8 signed letter permutations, multiplying by a rotated copy of the other relator or its inverse (all AC equivalences).
check: Matched by canonical form (rotation, inversion, 8 relabellings, relator order) independently by two sessions on 2026-09-28; both got these 47. AK(3) itself is in the set. No solved row matches. Coverage: starts of total length <= 26 only.
stable_ac: AK(3)'s stable status is also treated as open, so the sac- twins are blocked too.
independent_check_20260928: The team lead's audit of Lisitsa (arXiv 2501.18601) / Shehper et al. (arXiv 2408.15332 §3.5): 53 h_i moves (67 standard AC moves) take P = (ABaBAbaBBabAb, BAbbABabaBBa) to AK(3); replay tools/acc/ak3_p_to_ak3_replay.py passes. P lies in the acwindow-lean AK(3)-class walk (canonical form found among the 1,284,411 members), confirming the walk. The early paper's stable-triviality conclusion was withdrawn in the corrected article, so AK(3)'s stable status stays open and the sac- twins of these rows stay skipped. P itself is not a board row.
